land.text: the Liaoxi homeland of the Murong, whose chief held Jin titles (Duke of Liaodong, 321); Huang took the title of Prince of Yan on 23 November 337

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessors: Jin dynasty (266-420), Ran Wei, Later Zhao, Duan Qi; the last three are lands Yan conquered in 350-357 and are in the ledger as gains.

land.text: the Yan realm: Ye fell on 11 December 370 to Wang Meng's Qin army, Murong Wei captured

capitals.name: Jicheng (棘城), Liaoxi
capitals.note: Infobox 'Jicheng (棘城) 337-342'; coordinates a placement in Liaoxi, Liaoning (the page gives none).

capitals.name: Longcheng (Chaoyang)
capitals.note: 'The capital moved to Longcheng' in 342 (infobox 342-350); the identification with modern Chaoyang is the usual one, not the page's.

capitals.name: Jicheng (薊城, Beijing)
capitals.note: Jun 'moved the capital to Jicheng (modern Beijing) in 350'.

capitals.name: Yecheng (Ye)
capitals.note: 'Later in 357, Murong Jun moved the capital from Jicheng to Ye.'

rulers.name: Murong Jun
rulers.title: Prince of Yan; emperor from 352/353
rulers.note: The intro says 352, the infobox 4 January 353; the Murong Jun page 'winter 352' and 6 April 353 for the empress.

rulers.name: Murong Wei
rulers.note: Captured when Ye fell on 11 December 370.

correction.text: the Liaoxi and Liaodong homeland round Jicheng and (from 342) Longcheng, 337-349; Beijing and Hebei come in 350-352 by the ledger: 'From Liaoning, the Former Yan later conquered and ruled over Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong and Henan at its peak'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 337 shape (498,272 km2; 690,000 by the gazetteer's cells) holds the whole of Hebei (203,000 km2), Shandong (219,000), Beijing and Tianjin (38,000), 41,000 of Henan and 66,000 of Anhui and Jiangsu besides Liaoning (118,000): it is the 353 peak with parts cut off. The pages give Yan only Liaoning in 337-349 (Prince of Yan 337; Duan Liaoxi destroyed with Later Zhao in 338; Longcheng 342; Yuwen 344 and Buyeo 346 raids), Beijing and central Hebei in 350 and Ye in 352; Hebei and Shandong were Later Zhao's until then. The infobox has no area.

minus.text: the Cliopatria 353 shape without Shandong (Duan Qi, taken 357) and Henan (taken from Jin 359-365): 'Ran Wei' destroyed in 352 'established Former Yan as a regional power on the North China Plain'; the ledger adds Shandong (357) and Henan (365)
the Dai principality's core, 'five counties north of the mountain ranges' (Datong and Hohhot radii of the dai-sixteen-kingdoms dossier)

correction.text: the Cliopatria 353 shape without Shandong and Henan (as before) and without the Dai principality's core round Datong and Hohhot, which the Dai held until 376

keyframe_review.note: 353-366, 772,045 km2 (1,039,000 by the gazetteer's cells). Page checks: Hebei and Beijing 350-352 (Murong Jun page), Shandong 355-357, Henan from 359 and Luoyang 365 ('brought the empire to its peak'); Shanxi (182,000 km2 in the shape) is not on the page, whose peak list reads 'Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong and Henan' (probably Shanxi); the 66,000 km2 of Anhui and Jiangsu are not on it either: both kept unverified. No infobox area. fx-29 (F248): the Dai core is cut (268 cells of the shape, 159 of them Shanxi, 66 Inner Mongolia, 43 Hebei, were also the dai-sixteen-kingdoms dossier's). Former Yan page: 'From Liaoning, the Former Yan later conquered and ruled over Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong and Henan at its peak' (no Shanxi, Dai or Inner Mongolia named); Dai page: capital Shengle 340-376, 'Disestablished: 376' by Former Qin, a marriage alliance with Former Yan 'though relations were tense at times, leading to clashes'; the infobox's 'Vassal of ... Former Yan' carries no date or territory.

367-370: 772,045 km2, the 353 outline with Shandong and Henan, i.e. the peak after Luoyang (365). The Murong Ke death in 367 and Murong Ping's rise change nothing; Huan Wen's 369 invasion ends at Fangtou without a border change; Ye falls on 11 December 370 and Cliopatria's last year matches the page. fx-29 (F248): the Dai core is cut as in the 353 keyframe (Former Yan page's peak list: Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong, Henan; Dai page: Dai ended in 376 under Former Qin).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 367 shape without the Dai principality's core round Datong and Hohhot, which the Dai held until 376

ledger.note: 337: Murong Huang takes the title of Prince of Yan. 'Murong Huang's claim of the princely title was on 23 November 337' (infobox); 'through the support of his officials'; capital Jicheng (棘城) in Liaoxi.
342: the capital moves to Longcheng (infobox Longcheng 342-350).

region.text: Goguryeo: 'Former Yan invaded Goguryeo and sacked the capital Hwando, forcing their king Gogugwon into submission'

ledger.note: 342: Goguryeo is forced to submit. 'Later that year, Former Yan invaded Goguryeo and sacked the capital Hwando, forcing their king Gogugwon into submission.' The page does not call it vassalage or say how long it lasted.
350: Jicheng falls. 'In the spring of 350, Murong Jun launched the attack' on Later Zhao 'and quickly took Jicheng' (modern Beijing).
350: the capital moves to Jicheng (Beijing). 'Jun invaded the Central Plains and moved the capital to Jicheng (modern Beijing) in 350.'

region.text: commanderies in Ji Province (central Hebei), nearing Xiangguo

ledger.note: Winter 350: Ji Province. Jun 'quickly captured a number of commanderies in Ji Province' as Later Zhao collapsed. The page names Ji Province, not its boundary; the region is the Hebei and Tianjin part of Cliopatria's 353 outline.

region.text: Ye and the Ran Wei lands on the North China Plain

ledger.note: 352: Ran Wei ends at Ye. Murong Ke captured Ran Min at the Battle of Liantai in summer 352; then 'Former Yan forces captured Ran Zhi and Empress Dong, ending Ran Wei' (the Former Yan page: Ran Zhi surrendered at Ye). 'The destruction of Ran Wei established Former Yan as a regional power on the North China Plain.'

region.text: Shandong, round Guanggu (modern Qingzhou), the Duan Qi capital

ledger.note: 355: Murong Jun sends Murong Ke against Duan Kan. 'In 355, angered that his cousin Duan Kan (段龕), who was in control of modern Shandong ...' Murong Jun 'sent Murong Ke and Yang Wu against him'; 'In 356, despite the heavy fortifications that Duan's capital Guanggu had, Murong Ke sieged it, and after Duan's food supplies ran out, he was forced to surrender.' [Reviewer ea-03-b: the page dates the siege and surrender 356, not 355-357.]

356: Duan Qi surrenders. Murong Ke besieges Guanggu in 356 and Duan Kan is 'forced to surrender' when his food runs out (Murong Jun page); he is spared at first and executed in 357. The Former Yan page: Ke defeated 'the remnants of the Later Zhao, including the Duan Qi state in Shandong'. [Reviewer ea-03-b: year 357 corrected to 356.]
356: Duan Qi falls at Guanggu; Shandong is Yan's. [Reviewer ea-03-b: year 357 corrected to 356 (Murong Jun page: siege and surrender in 356, execution in 357).]
357: the capital moves to Ye. 'Later in 357, Murong Jun moved the capital from Jicheng to Ye.'

region.text: Henan, south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 359: Jin forces defeated in Henan. The victory over Zhuge You and Xie Wan 'allowed Former Yan to gradually take over the modern Henan region'.
365: Murong Ke takes Luoyang. 'In 365, he captured the ancient capital, Luoyang, from Jin and brought the empire to its peak.'
365: Henan is Yan's. The Murong Jun page has Yan taking Henan 'gradually' from 359, with no later date; Luoyang's fall in 365 is the last step on the Former Yan page.
365: the Jin lose Henan with Luoyang.

region.text: Fangtou on the Yellow River, where Huan Wen was defeated

ledger.note: 369: Huan Wen invades. 'Huan Wen invaded. Murong Chui defeated him at the Battle of Fangtou.' The page does not locate Fangtou; the Anyang disc is my placement (Fangtou is on the Yellow River in the Ye-Luoyang corridor, which the page does not say).
369: Huan Wen is beaten at Fangtou; no border moves.

region.text: the realm, from the Luchuan battlefield to Ye

ledger.note: 370: Wang Meng attacks. 'Wang Meng destroyed the main Yan army at the Battle of Luchuan. Qin forces reached Ye.'
370: any submission of Goguryeo ends with the Yan. The page says nothing of the relation after 342.
11 December 370: Ye falls. 'Qin forces reached Ye, Murong Wei was captured, and Ye fell on 11 December 370.'

region.text: the Yan realm, taken by Former Qin

ledger.note: 11 December 370: the Former Yan ends. Ye falls to Former Qin and Murong Wei is captured (infobox: 'disestablished 370, the fall of Yecheng on 11 December').

wars.name: Yan and Later Zhao against the Duan of Liaoxi
wars.outcome: The allies conquered the Duan tribe in Liaoxi; Later Zhao then 'betrayed Yan' and besieged Jicheng (棘城) in vain.
wars.note: The Duan's land and its fate are not on the page; no Yan border change is recorded.

wars.name: Yan invasion of Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Hwando sacked and King Gogugwon forced into submission.

wars.name: Yan campaigns against the Yuwen and Buyeo
wars.outcome: The Yuwen power base destroyed (344); Buyeo invaded and its king Hyeon captured (346).
wars.note: Neither page names land annexed; the Murong Jun page adds a 344 expedition against Dai in which 'no significant battle occurred'.

wars.name: Yan conquest of Later Zhao and Ran Wei lands
wars.outcome: Jicheng taken in spring 350; commanderies in Ji Province in winter 350; Ran Min captured in summer 352 and Ye taken, ending Ran Wei.

wars.name: Yan conquest of Duan Qi
wars.outcome: Murong Ke besieged Guanggu; Duan Kan surrendered and was executed in 357.

wars.name: Yan-Jin war for Henan
wars.outcome: Yan beat Zhuge You and Xie Wan in 359 and took Henan gradually; Luoyang fell in 365.

wars.name: Battle of Fangtou
wars.outcome: Murong Chui defeated Huan Wen's invasion; no border changed. Chui then defected to Former Qin after Murong Ping tried to kill him.

wars.name: Former Qin conquest of Former Yan
wars.outcome: Wang Meng destroyed the main Yan army at Luchuan and took Ye on 11 December 370; Murong Wei captured.

certainty.note: Commandery and provincial frontiers on the North China Plain and Liaoxi; no treaty lines on the pages opened; the Henan front 359-365 and the Goguryeo and Buyeo edges are the softest.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Former Yan', 3 shapes, 337..370, all reviewed. Wikidata Q1472004 is shared with 'yan' (the Warring States Yan, -1046..-204): two different states 600 years apart; Cliopatria's Wikidata mapping is wrong, and Q1472004 is kept in identity only as Cliopatria's value.
Cliopatria errors: (1) the 337-352 shape (498,272 km2) already holds Hebei, Shandong, Beijing and Tianjin, which Later Zhao held until 350-357, so it overlaps the later-zhao dossier; (2) the 353 shape has Shandong and Henan five and twelve years early, and Shanxi, Anhui and Jiangsu parts that no page opened gives. Corrections are baselines plus ledger gains (350 Jicheng, 350 Ji Province, 352 Ye, 357 Shandong, 365 Henan).
Unsettled: Shanxi (the page says 'Shaanxi' for the peak); Anhui and Jiangsu; the extent of the Yuwen and Buyeo conquests (344, 346: raids or annexations); whether Goguryeo stayed a vassal after 342; the location of Fangtou; the exact coordinates of 棘城 (Jicheng in Liaoxi) and Longcheng.
Counterparts needing dossiers: ran-wei (Ran Wei, 350-352), duan-qi (Duan Qi), Yuwen, Buyeo (jk-02 or ea-03-x); goguryeo (jk-02) holds the 342 sack. Western-jin and former-qin are written by other parts.
